'''Malcolm Jean Ahmed Cazalon''' (born 27 August 2001) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Cholet Basket]] of [[LNB Pro A]].

==Early life==
Cazalon was born in [[Roanne]], France, where his father [[Laurent Cazalon]] was a professional basketball player.<ref name="abreu">{{cite web |last1=De Abreu |first1=Dylan |title=Espoirs Pro A : le fils de Laurent Cazalon se montre face à Nanterre |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/383624/espoirs-pro-a-le-fils-de-laurent-cazalon-se-montre-face-a-nanterre/ |publisher=Basket Europe |accessdate=20 July 2019 |language=French |date=7 November 2016}}</ref> He began playing basketball as a child with local club [[Chorale Roanne Basket|Chorale Roanne]].<ref name="roche">{{cite web |last1=Roche |first1=Jules |title=Un Roannais idéalement placé dans les prévisions de la Draft 2020 ! |url=https://www.parlonssports.fr/2018/11/un-roannais-idealement-place-dans-les-previsions-de-la-draft-2020/ |publisher=Parlons Sports |accessdate=20 July 2019 |language=French |date=12 November 2018 |archive-date=20 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720135926/https://www.parlonssports.fr/2018/11/un-roannais-idealement-place-dans-les-previsions-de-la-draft-2020/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2017, he moved to [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]], with whom he played in the LNB Espoirs under-21 league.<ref name="gabriel">{{cite web |last1=Pantel-Jouve |first1=Gabriel |title=Malcolm Cazalon, l'animal que l'ASVEL veut dompter |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-espoirs/malcolm-cazalon--l-animal-que-l-asvel-veut-dompter.html |publisher=BeBasket |accessdate=20 July 2019 |language=French |date=14 March 2017 |archive-date=4 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504162540/https://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-espoirs/malcolm-cazalon--l-animal-que-l-asvel-veut-dompter.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===JL Bourg / Leuven Bears (2018–2020)===
On 23 August 2018, Cazalon signed a three-year contract with [[JL Bourg Basket|JL Bourg]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], the top professional league in France.<ref name="rutard">{{cite web|first=Sacha|last=Rutard|title=Malcolm Cazalon a signé pour trois saisons à la JL Bourg|url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/438978/malcolm-cazalon-a-signe-pour-trois-saisons-a-la-jl-bourg/|work=Basket Europe|date=28 August 2018|access-date=20 July 2019|language=French}}</ref> On 19 July 2019, he was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] to [[Leuven Bears]] of the [[Pro Basketball League]] (PBL) in Belgium.<ref name="leuven">{{cite news|first=Emiliano|last=Carchia|title=Malcolm Cazalon verso il prestito ai Leuven Bears|url=https://sportando.basketball/malcolm-cazalon-verso-il-prestito-ai-leuven-bears/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=19 July 2019|access-date=20 July 2019|language=Italian}}</ref>

===Mega Basket (2020–2023)===
On 10 March 2020, Cazalon signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Bemax]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Emiliano|last=Carchia|title=Mega Bemax signs Malcolm Cazalon|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/mega-bemax-signs-malcolm-cazalon/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=10 March 2020|access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Following the 2020–21 season, Cazalon declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]]. On July 19, 2021, he withdrew his name from consideration for the 2021 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA announces 51 early entry candidates withdraw from 2021 Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-51-early-entry-candidates-withdraw-from-2021-draft|website=NBA.com|date=20 July 2021|access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref> In April 2022, Cazalon declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nikola Jović izlazi na NBA draft|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/nba/vesti.php?yyyy=2022&mm=04&dd=11&nav_id=2138077|website=b92.net|date=11 April 2022|access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref> Later, he withdrew his name from consideration for the 2022 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|title=24 early-entry candidates withdraw from NBA Draft 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/news/24-early-entry-candidates-withdraw-from-nba-draft-2022|website=NBA.com|date=15 June 2022|access-date=23 June 2022}}</ref> On 4 July 2022, Cazalon signed a one-year contract extension with Mega Basket.<ref>{{cite web|title=Malkolm Kazalon ostaje u Megi|url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/malkolm-kazalon-ostaje-u-megi/424313|website=MozzartSport.com|date=4 July 2022|access-date=4 July 2022}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2023–2024)===
After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Cazalon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) on 2 July 2023<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed guards Jared Rhoden and Malcolm Cazalon to two-way contracts. Per team policy, terms of the agreements were not disclosed.|number=1675530509244411904|user=Pistons_PR|date=2 July 2023|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> and joined them for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS 2023 NBA 2K24 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2023/vegas/team/1610612765/pistons|website=NBA.com|access-date=8 October 2023}}</ref> However, he  was waived on 21 February 2024.<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Pistons Waive Malcolm Cazalon|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/02/pistons-to-waive-malcolm-cazalon.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=21 February 2024|access-date=23 February 2024}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2024)===
On 24 February 2024, Cazalon joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire Malcolm Cazalon|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-malcolm-cazalon|website=NBA.com|date=24 February 2024|access-date=24 February 2024}}</ref>

===SIG Strasbourg (2024–2025)===
On 6 December 2024, Cazalon signed with [[SIG Strasbourg]] of the [[LNB Élite]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Malik out 3 mois – Malcolm Cazalon arrive en aide|url=https://sigstrasbourg.fr/index.php/2024/12/malik-out-3-mois-malcolm-cazalon-arrive-en-aide|website=SIGStrasbourg.fr|date=6 December 2024|access-date=6 December 2024|language=French}}</ref>

===Bilbao Basket (2025)===
On February 17, 2025, Cazalon was announced as a new player [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. He signed a contract for the remainder of the [[2024-25 ACB season|2024-25 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Malcolm Cazalon firma con Surne Bilbao Basket hasta final de temporada|url=https://bilbaobasket.biz/malcolm-cazalon-firma-con-surne-bilbao-basket-hasta-final-de-temporada/|website=bilbaobasket.biz|date=17 February 2025|access-date=16 March 2025|language=es}}</ref>

=== Merkezefendi Basket (2025–2026) ===
On August 3, 2025, he signed with [[Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket|Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=merkezefendigsk |number=1956744806207472068 |title=Malcolm Cazalon Yukatel Merkezefendi’de}}</ref>

=== Cholet Basket (2026–present) ===
On August 24, 2026, he signed with [[Cholet Basket]] of [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite Instagram |user=cholet_basket |postid=Dcam4DDjmvj |title=Malcolm Cazalon remplace Caleb Daniels ! |date=August 24, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Cazalon missed the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]], Montenegro, in which [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]] won the gold medal, with a knee injury.<ref name="fiba">{{cite web |title=France's new Three Musketeer heroes: Hayes, Cazalon, Maledon |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/news/france-s-new-three-musketeer-heroes-hayes-cazalon-maledon |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=20 July 2019 |date=7 July 2018}}</ref> At the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Argentina]], he averaged 16.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game, helping France win the silver medal.<ref name="fiba2">{{cite web |title=Malcolm Cazalon (FRA)'s profile - FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup 2018 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Malcolm-Cazalon |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=20 July 2019}}</ref>
